title: Agent Memory — Virtual Context and Memory Paging
service: memgpt: a MemGPT-style memory layer with a token-budgeted main context, cited archival memory and the five memory tools, a SQLite archive, BM25 archival search with recall@k, an interrupt-driven pager with a rolling summary, and typed nested core memory

parts.lesson_anchor: Two tiers; The interrupt pattern (the canonical memory tool surface); Where this pattern goes wrong: Citation loss; Exercise 1 (a token cap approximated with len(text.split()) * 1.3); code/main.py MainContext, ArchivalStore.search, MemoryTools
planted_bugs: MemoryTools.archival_memory_insert passes only tags to ArchivalStore.insert, so every record is cited s0#0; it surfaces one call later, in the citations archival_memory_search prints
core_memory_replace uses str.replace on every occurrence although the docstring requires old to occur exactly once; replacing ava in 'name=ava, stack=java' also turns java into jeva
MainContext.tokens estimates the joined text, ceil(total words * 1.3), instead of summing approx_tokens per message, so three two-word messages cost 8 instead of 9 and one message too many stays
ArchivalStore.search re-tokenizes every record on every query
parts.timing_assert: 150 queries over 20000 records under 0.08 s (the shipped scan takes 1.38 to 1.39 s on this machine, a pre-tokenized full scan 0.17 to 0.21 s, the inverted index 3.5 to 4.6 ms)
parts.overfix_guard: scores stay the exact Jaccard of distinct tokens split by tokenize (postings per occurrence, a query counted with repeats, stripped punctuation or another score all fail); ties keep insertion order (a set of candidates, heapq.nlargest on the score, ranking by score alone or by rid string all fail on the large archive; ranking by turn fails on one fact stored at turn 9 of s1 and turn 2 of s3); the same text from two sessions stays two records; a context costing exactly max_tokens is not paged; the newest message always stays; core sections stay out of max_tokens; paged-out messages stay searchable
parts.deviation: The suggested 20000 records x 300 queries would make the shipped scan run about 3 s, at the 3 s ceiling, so the timing uses 150 queries (about 1.4 s). Pre-tokenizing alone does not reach the 0.08 s limit; the fix is the inverted index the suggestion names. The class already budgets tokens, so the token bug is the estimate of the joined text against the docstring's per-message sum. The replace check covers repeated occurrences only; the empty old string belongs to lesson 08.

parts.lesson_anchor: Two tiers: external context is unbounded and searchable; Citation loss: store session ID and turn ID with every archival write; outputs/skill-virtual-memory.md (records carry id, text, tags, session_id, turn_id; expose delete(id))
parts.exactness: records come back equal and typed after a reopen: text with non-ASCII, a newline and a trailing space; tags as an ordered tuple, including a tag with a comma and capitals (lang:zh-Hans,en) and an empty tuple; session_id a str and turn_id an int, the types checked in passing (40.0 == 40) since the module docstring declares the turn_id column INTEGER
traps: INTEGER PRIMARY KEY without AUTOINCREMENT, COUNT(*) + 1, MAX(seq) + 1 or an in-memory counter reuse a deleted id
insert not committed, or committed only in close(), while a second connection reads
tags joined with commas, returned as a list, stored sorted or lowercased
text stripped
records ordered by rid string, which breaks after a999, or by turn_id, which each session numbers on its own
records not loaded on open, or loaded without _keep so search has no index
delete that leaves the record in memory, leaves the search index on old positions, is not committed, or ignores an unknown id
CREATE TABLE without IF NOT EXISTS
parts.deviation: delete(rid) is added (the lesson's skill file asks for delete(id)) so that id reuse can be tested; citations are the reason ids must never be reused. The module docstring declares the turn_id column INTEGER, so SQLite type affinity, which other lessons in this phase test, is not one of this part's traps; the test still checks the types in passing.

parts.lesson_anchor: Exercise 2 (implement BM25 with term frequency and inverse document frequency, measure recall on a toy fact set against the token-overlap baseline); Build It: the archival store scores by token overlap
traps: classic idf, negative for a token in most records
empty records left out of N or avgdl
tf counted once per record, or document frequency counted per occurrence
a repeated query token counted once
tokens split differently from the archive (punctuation stripped, no lowercasing)
zero scores returned, top_k ignored, ties reversed or ordered by rid instead of the order of the list BM25 was built from
division by zero for an empty archive or a single empty record
recall as a hit rate, divided by k or by min(k, relevant), skipping cases without results, or using the search function's own default top_k (also when cut to k)
a case with no relevant records, also among other cases, or an empty list of cases, accepted instead of a ValueError
parts.integration: the same 12 facts in an ArchivalStore and in BM25: recall@1 is 4/9 for token overlap and 7/9 for BM25, recall@3 6.5/9 and 8/9, recall@5 8/9 for both; one case has no query token in its relevant record and stays unfound by both

parts.lesson_anchor: The interrupt pattern (the runtime serves a memory call and the result splices into the next turn); Exercise 1 (compact the oldest messages into a summary when the cap is exceeded); Build It: MainContext auto-compacts the oldest messages; conversation_search scans past turns
parts.wire_format: NDJSON events memory_pressure, page_out and summary, one per yield, decided by the test's per-chunk json.loads, join, splitlines and json.loads
traps: missing newline, blank lines, pretty-printed JSON or bytes

pressure on every message above the line, re-armed only by a page-out, once per stream, not at exactly warn_tokens, measured from the size right after the previous push, or raised when the context already sat at warn_tokens
pressure reported after paging out, or a message's events yielded together
summary awaited before page_out is reported
every message read before paging
one page-out per message, so a grown summary leaves the context over budget
summary left out of the budget, or approx_tokens rounded
summarize given only the new messages, the summary appended instead of replaced, or summarize not awaited
paged-out messages dropped from recall or added twice
every older message paged out at once
a pager that keeps paging when only the newest message is left
parts.deviation: The lesson names the interrupt pattern and summary compaction but no warning threshold, so memory_pressure, warn_tokens and the crossing rule are this service's design, stated in the page_stream docstring. The summary is ctx.summary rather than a message, and the summarizer is an async function the test supplies. A second short stream checks the exact warn_tokens boundary and a message bigger than the whole budget, read through a bounded consumer so a looping pager fails instead of hanging.

parts.lesson_anchor: Exercise 5 (from flat strings to typed sections); Key Terms: core memory is named sections pinned inside the main context; code/main.py MainContext.render and core_memory_append
traps: limits or usage counted in bytes
a group's usage counting only the text sections right under it, or every text section whose path merely starts with the group's (human_notes counted under human)
only the section, only the section and its parent, or only the groups above the text section checked
the outermost limit reported instead of the innermost, or the section named without its dotted path
the separating space left out of the size
a write that lands exactly on a limit refused
a refused write that keeps the new text
replace on every occurrence, or without the limit check
paths: an empty segment, a path running past a text section, case-insensitive names, text written to a group
render sorted like the lesson's render, empty sections left out, or an empty text section with a trailing colon
parts.deviation: The lesson points Exercise 5 at the research repo's core-memory JSON schema without describing it, so the schema shape, the (used/limit) render and the innermost-section error are this service's own design, stated in the TypedCore docstrings. Lesson 08 owns flat block limits; this part is about limits that nest.
